To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

risky discounts are more popular on a per-item than on a per-purchasing basis, and that this preference is driven by the greater excitement of multiple discount gambles and by a partly incorrect perception that these gambles are less risky than expected.

consumers prefer per-item over per- purchase risky discounts because they perceive per-item discounts as more exciting than per- purchase risky ones, because they perceive per-purchase discounts as more risky than per-item risky ones, and because they adopt a narrow mindset when evaluating per-purchase risky discounts.

consumers prefer to receive discounts on a per-item basis because they expect to receive more savings, because they perceive that they have greater control and are not at the mercy of the retailer, and because they experience more excitement and enjoyment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the number of discount gambles in a series on consumer preference for and perceptions of risky discounts.
the effects of discount format on consumer preferences.
the question of whether risky discounts are more attractive if the consumer receives them on a per-purchasing or per-item basis and why this is the case.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
consumers prefer risky discounts on a “per-item” basis, because this option offers a higher expected utility.
risky discounting is more attractive on a per-item basis because of the greater excitement, but less attractive because of the lower expected value of savings.
risky discounts are preferred when they are offered on a per-item basis, and that this preference can be explained in terms of the savings distribution and the excitement involved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
risky discounts should be offered on a per-item basis, because this is the format that consumers prefer and the one that provides the greatest consumer satisfaction and perceived value.
risky discounts are more appealing when they are applied on a per-item basis.
people prefer to gamble on a per-item basis because it provides more excitement and more chances for a high outcome.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the choice of a risky discount format should not be determined by the expected value of the savings alone, but also by the consumer’s preferences for the various properties of the savings distributions.

the choice between risky discounts on a series of items or purchases is not trivial and that consumers should be made aware that their preferences may be driven by incorrect perceptions of the savings distribution and the excitement of multiple discount gambles rather than by the actual expected value of savings.
the format of a discount offer can have a strong influence on consumers’ preferences, even when these offers have the same expected value.
